text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Decision by Telecommunications Authority of Singapore to license additional basic telephone operators from 2002 will benefit both business community and public, says Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan.
- Talented students in Britain being offered golden hellos worth thousands of pounds by universities keen to attract high-flyers, particularly to science and engineering courses.
- Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will go to Egypt for talks on ending Middle East peacemaking crisis that deepened with suicide bombing in Jerusalem street market.
- Din still there but technician Yap Eng Kwang said getting out of his Chander Road flat on Sundays now easier.
- Bank Negara Malaysia, country's central bank, announces powerful restriction aimed at curbing swap transactions to beat currency speculators.
- Tecommunication Authority of Singapore has identified and addressed potential bottlenecks which may plague new basic telephone licensees in order to "prevent any abuse of market power".
- APPLE Computer Singapore -- which retrenched about 350 employees this year -- has lost managing director Peter Tan, who has resigned to join local firm JIT Engineering.
- Local stock market may be in doldrums but average premium enjoyed by foreign shares over local counterparts has soared to 53 percent, highest since foreign shares introduced nine years ago.

- Thailand has hammered out terms of economic rescue package with International Monetary Fund aimed at bolstering country's declining foreign reserves and bringing investment into cash-strapped economy, says Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee.
- Wife of rogue trader Nick Leeson who caused collapse of Britain's oldest investment bank, Barings, said to be taking steps to end six-year marriage.
- British authorities investigating allegations Hong Kong's last Governor, Chris Patten, leaked secret documents, says government.
- Counter's upgrading from Sesdaq to main board does not always come with price hike even though many things turn in its favour from move.
